memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Deeply moved at the sight of his brother, Joseph hurried out and looked for a place to weep. He went into his private room and wept there. After he had washed his face, he came out and, controlling himself, said, 'Serve the food.'" - Gen 43:30-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The sight of Benjamin is more than Joseph can bear. "Deeply moved at the sight of his brother," he has to hurry from the room to hide his tears, weeping alone in private before washing his face and composing himself to return. Beneath his powerful, controlled exterior, a flood of love and longing pours out. He weeps for his brother, for all the lost years, for the family he has missed so deeply.

This is one of the most human and tender moments in Joseph's story. Here is a man of immense power and self-control, yet love breaks through and moves him to tears. He is not made of stone. All the authority of Egypt could not harden his heart against the love he felt for his own family.

There is something reassuring in this for us. Deep emotion, even tears, is not weakness; it is often the mark of a loving heart. Joseph was strong, yet he wept. Jesus Himself wept at the tomb of His friend Lazarus (John 11:35). To be moved to tears by love or grief is not something to be ashamed of; it reflects a heart that truly cares.

Notice, too, Joseph's balance: he allowed himself to feel deeply, weeping in private, and then composed himself to do what needed to be done. There is a time to let our emotions flow and a time to steady ourselves and carry on. May we, like Joseph, neither suppress our God-given emotions nor be ruled by them, but feel deeply and then move forward in love.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I see deep emotion and tears as weakness or as a mark of love?
2. Am I able both to feel deeply and to steady myself to act?
3. Where might God be softening my heart with love or grief?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that even tears can flow from a loving heart. Help me neither to suppress the emotions You have given me nor to be ruled by them, but to feel deeply and to move forward in love. Amen.
